subject: Sealed Edge: next steps for on-prem qualification & ops
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@genomix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — sealed / air-gapped on-prem qualification

Hi Samira — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of constraints you shared
- Must be fully air-gapped (no persistent internet egress from the inference appliance).
- Typical maintenance windows: one quarterly 2–4 hour window; emergency patches by coordinated ship of signed images.
- Key management: customer-managed HSM preferred; otherwise we need a signed KMS integration plan.
- HW procurement lead time: 10–12 weeks (you flagged internal procurement approvals).
- Expected throughput: ~25 concurrent inference sessions, median seq len ~1024, occasional burst to 4k tokens.

Options we reviewed (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to test but rejected for production due to data residency/air-gap needs.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated): possible interim for dev/test, still requires egress for telemetry — not ideal for sealed production.
- Private (sealed on-prem appliance / VPC): target for production. Needs offline upgrade flow, signed binaries, and onsite maintenance model.

Immediate asks / action items
1) Please send your site network diagram (existing draft ok) and any outbound-controlled egress policies. Ideally before 2028-03-28.
2) Confirm the HSM/KMS approach (vendor + model) or let us know if Redwood should plan for HSM integration workshops.
3) Share the procurement timeline and preferred on-site dates for a survey (we suggested week of Apr 8).

Attachments: Genomix_OnPrem_Requirements_v2.pdf (Redwood side draft of requirements from today’s call)

Proposed next step from Redwood: we’ll produce a short decision log mapping the required HW, upgrade flow, and ops plan (sealed appliance: image signing, transport media, and patch cadence). Ben and Laura are looped for ops/hardware scope.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM serving
From: Samira Khan <samira@genomix.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@bioprod.co>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — sealed / air-gapped on-prem qualification

Avery — great summary, thank you. A few clarifications and answers from our side: 

- We confirm sealed deployment requirement for prod. Dev/test can live on a dedicated cloud seat but production must be air-gapped.
- HSM: we run Thales Luna in most locations; I will confirm model numbers by EOD Friday.
- Maintenance: quarterly patches are fine; for security-critical patches we need a documented offline upgrade flow and a signed binary distribution process.
- Procurement: target order Q2 final approval; site readiness windows open starting Apr 15.

I attached our current network diagram (site-network-diagram_v1.png). It shows the separation zones and the one-way data diode we plan for telemetry export (we still need to verify legal constraints).

Two asks for Redwood: 
1) Can you provide a short explanation of the offline upgrade workflow (how Redwood ensures signed images, verification on boot, and rollback)? A 1–page diagram or checklist would be perfect.
2) Your standard MoU / Statement of Work template for sealed appliance pilots — we can share with procurement.

Happy to hop on a short call next week if useful; otherwise we’ll aim to send the HSM details and confirm procurement cadence by Fri.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Ops, Genomix Therapeutics

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Genomix sealed-edge decision log and pre-survey asks

Ben/Laura — looping you with Samira’s responses and the network diagram. Draft decision log below (will send external-friendly version after your confirm):

Decision log (draft)
- Target mode: Private Sealed Appliance (air-gapped) — customer-owned HW running Redwood sealed image.
- Upgrade model: Signed images + checksum verification at boot. Transport via encrypted removable media couriered to site; on-site engineer performs install and signs install ticket.
- Telemetry: one-way exports via physical diode to a staging host; limited telemetry packages only, full logs remain on-prem unless explicit export permission.
- KMS: integrate with customer HSM (Thales) for disk encryption keys; Redwood does not hold customer master keys.
- SLA expectations: propose 99.5% uptime for appliance, with a scheduled quarterly maintenance SLA window and emergency patch response time SLA to be negotiated.

Questions for ops/hw follow-up
- Ben: confirm HW SKU footprint (GPU, NVMe, RAM) to support 25 concurrent sessions @ 1k tokens median. If we propose the Redwood sealed SKU-XL, what spares do we require?
- Laura: propose an on-site survey checklist and estimate of engineer-days for install + validation.

If both of you OK, I’ll send the external version with the MoU draft and propose Apr 17–19 for an on-site readiness survey.

Avery
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@genomix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — sealed / air-gapped on-prem qualification

Hi Samira — quick follow to confirm next steps and share items we promised during the call. I’ve included Ben and Laura for scheduling and ops detail.

1) On-site readiness survey: proposed window Apr 17–19 (engineer team: 2 people, 1 day on-site). Please confirm preferred date.
2) Draft MoU / pilot SOW: https://drive.redwood.com/Genomix/SealedEdge/requirements (link to Redwood draft). I attached a Word copy for procurement (Redwood_MoU_SealedEdge_Draft.docx).
3) Offline upgrade flow: short checklist below (we’ll provide a diagram in the drive link):
   - Build signed image in secure build environment.
   - Produce signed checksum file and sign with Redwood release key.
   - Transfer image on sealed encrypted media; manifest & signature accompany media.
   - On-site engineer verifies signature against manifest before flashing.
   - Post-flash integrity check; if failure, automated rollback to previous image stored in read-only partition.
   - Install ticket and hash values returned to Genomix security team for audit.

4) HSM: once you confirm Thales model we’ll schedule a short KMS integration scoping call with our security engineering team.

Attachments: Redwood_MoU_SealedEdge_Draft.docx

If you’re good with the Apr 17–19 survey, we’ll block time and circulate an engineer readiness checklist (power, rack space, KVM access, local contact).

Best — Avery
